Horses are a big part of the Jeju culture  and Jeju Horse Park is a pretty cool place. Its museum includes many photographs  artifacts and a video telling the story of the Jeju "ma " or pony  which is descended from the ponies brought to the island by Mongol invaders. The island was considered a good place to raise horses  and the Mongols used it as such. At the park  you can also ride the horses. There is a great giftshop with lots of local handmade items. Children or even adults can make related crafts in an activity room. The building itself is round like a ger  the traditional nomadic tents used by the Mongols. The top deck includes a fabulous 360-degree view of the "oreums" (small cinder-cones or parasitic volcanoes) that literally ring the area of the park. Inside the railing  an artist has painted the oreums  along with their names. So  you can know exactly which oreums you are viewing. There are also some actual Mongolian gers (also known as yurts in other nomadic cultures). I believe tourists can actually spend the night in one of the gers. One thing to consider: If you want to visit  you must either have your own transportation or go with someone who does. It's kind of far from anywhere  and bus service may not operate in that area. Likewise  taxis don't just happen by. But  it is a beautiful area and interesting for the entire family We visited in the spring  and there were also lots of colorful wildflowers. Plan to spend a few hours there  especially if you will ride the horses.

This is a gallery that a late photographer  Kim younggap  in his last days with Lou Gehrig's disease  established to store his films and photographs. This used to be an abandoned primary school. The best thing I liked about visiting this gallery was how he arranged this island's native rocks in his garden. Native rocks of Jeju islands are very very dark. Any color you bring against it shines. The garden makes you see it  and I think that's what he wanted to say in his garden. Check out the photographs. I think it is eye opening.

We have fun taking photos here even some miniatures looked old and not properly maintained. It would be such nice place to introduce the world famous building and attractions to your kids (and to adult as well). I wish they add more models to the park and revamp the old ones. Nevertheless  it was fun enough for us. Make sure to go early as when there are too many people  they might disturb you while taking photos.Admission fee for adult: approx. KRW9000

This miniature park is more for children & the young. Needless to say  my little nephew & myself still had fun photo-taking & running around. I wish there were more miniatures to see. But still worth a visit if you haven't travelled half of the world yet

i was excited to visit this park. unfortunately the park did not meet expectation. most of the models look fake  poorly maintained. maybe this park suitable for school kids to introduce them to the famous architecture. i really hope they do something to make sure visitors enjoy this miniature theme park. anyways  the concept is good. but not the models.

This miniature park had all the famous attractions from around the world which was great for viewing  especially when we haven't had the chance to see the real thing. However  you could see the place was a bit old and definitely needed some maintenance. So this place is definitely not for the fussy  but still worth a visit if you had time.
The park was poorly maintained  the water in the pond was murky and had many fallen leaves. The minatures looked so fake and some had paint chips. Give this a miss.

lots of countries miniatures but they looked so lame and not real.. a few cartoon figurines were okmy daughter liked the smurf village though some paints were chipped off here and therenot worth the visit though
You can't even get to the miniatures to take any cool pics. They are surrounded by hedges  which also ruins any pictures taken at scale.

We invite you to 'Figure Museum Jeju'  full of fantastic movie figures and statues! There are tons of high quality exhibits! Action figures  movie statues  life size statues  upcycling arts  game statues  etc. Everybody can enjoy and have fun here with figures from movies and games and animations.
Great for Marvel fans and it has some cool displays. It only takes about 30 minutes to see everything which makes the 12 000 KRW ticket price quite steep.

To be honest the place is very pretty and there is a tangerine picking farm inside (Jeju tangeries are famous in Korea) but I found the place pricey  and I have seen some animals there but I am not sure in which condition they live under. Then after I left I learned that they do pigs shows there and I don't feel really good about that.

Visited this place in Feb19 and was quite appalled by the treatment of the animals. The rabbits were allowed to roam within an enclosed area accessible to visitors. However there is no one monitoring that the rabbits are treated properly. The living conditions of the animals are filthy. The absolute horror was the black pig show. What's so entertaining about forcing terrified black pigs down a water slide?? Tasteless entertainment with no educational value. Paying the entrance fee of 13000won per person  I would expect some of it to be channeled to upkeep the living conditions of the animals. The blooms in the park were alright with spots for Instagram pictures but nothing spectacular.

Visited the park in Feb. Pretty blooms of camellia and cherry blossoms. Unfortunately the park keeps animals such as rabbits and pigs. The rabbits are not kept in proper conditions. More appalling is a black pig show where pigs are made to run up a ramp and slide down a very steep 1.5 storey slope. Not sure how any one can find this "show" entertaining. What do children learn about such a performance where animals are at risk of injury for the amusement of humans? Ghastly place. Stay away unless taking Instagram pictures in fake settings are your thing.

This park has a trail  insect specimens  pig show  petting zoo and several activities such as horse riding and tangerine picking.It is a good excursion place for everybody especially for family.

Seashell and coral art in their fascinating and natural colors. The seashells' mysterious world under the sea-- as designed by several artists. (is this a title. It was a rainy day out  so decided to check out indoor activities  def a lot of cool stuff here  smaller museum
Part museum  part art gallery and totally worth a visit. The shells are wonderfully displayed in a variety of artistic designs that enhance the viewing experience. Absolutely worth a visit.

I loved this museum so much! The seashells and paintings exhibited at this museum is awesome and seriously beautiful. Everything that you see in and around this museum is so artistic and shows so much of passion in it. The cafe within the vicinity is equally beautiful that offers good coffee and bread too!

Visit this place even if you not interested or lover of sea shells at least to recognise the sheer efforts put in by Ms Myeong Yeon Sook  the director of this museum and owner of this place. This museum which has over 7 800 variety and accounting to more than millions of sea shells originating in Jeju and the world is the brain child of Ms Sook and master Metal craftsman Kwon Oh-Kyun.The beauty of these sea shells are to be seen to be believed. They have been arranged and displayed so artistically that one may easily mistake it as a painting.One may not see much of visitors around  but this really helps as we go around enjoying the magic of nature.Entrance fee is a bit high  but really worth it  considering the efforts put in to bring this huge collection of sea shells under one roof and creating the world's first seashell museum.

Jeju has tonnes of 'museums' to draw in cash from tourists. Most of these are silly  man-made museums having no connection whatsoever to Jeju or even Korea. It is almost a sin to spend time in these museums while in Jeju  instead of enjoying the scenery outdoors.However I would reallly recommend a stop at the seashell museum if you have an hour to spare in the Seogwipo area. The labor of love of 1 woman  this place houses a staggering collection of shells from all over the world  crafted into stunning displays. Seashells so pretty  its hard to believe they are real..but they are.There's also a small shop to purchase souvenirs if you'd like but they don't pressure you. Also attached is a cafe.Close by to a bus stop.

We loved looking at the shells collected from all over the world. They were artistically arranged. It was well worth the $6.00 entrance fee and I received pearl stud earrings for free. The gift shop was expensive and bordered on tacky. The few shells for sale were very expensive  $68.00 for a small shell.
I really enjoy this place spend almost 2 hours here. Should come to visit if you stay in Seogwipo  Jeju city

It's part of our Jeju tour we stopped by.Beautiful collections spread throughout several floors. Lots of nice handiwork. Didn't have much time to view but for those who are interested in these kind of stuff it's a must see  otherwise half an hour visit would be plenty.There's also restroom and cafe on premise.

This is the most beautiful museum I have ever visited - absolutely packed with three floors of seashell art. When we visited there was no one else there at all! I have no idea why - but I probably wouldn't have enjoyed it as much if it was so busy. It was a bit more expensive than expected  probably because it doesn't get as many visitors  but it was well worth it and I got a free pair of earrings! Definitely go - they have a cafe too.

There is nearly no advertisement for this museum in the city. I saw the sign at the traffic and wanted to give it a try. The building is so small that when i arrived I thought it will be a quick tiny event. But once you are inside you will be amazed by the beauty and the variety of seashells. Most of the explanations are in Korean but still nothing can stop you to enjoy this museum. At the roof  there is a giant shell  which you can go in and have a photo. There is also a small shop where you can buy gifts to your loved ones and something for yourself too.

This museum provided so much variety and information from around the globe. Kids would get bored but if you enjoy art and seeing the natural beauty of the ocean than this is a good place to come. There are also an abundance of decently priced souvenirs and a cute Cafe! My wife also received free silver pearl earrings upon entry!
Nice to see the different types of seashell. However if you are short of time  it is okay to miss the place...

I took my girlfriend here as she absolutely loves all things aquatic  especially shells  and she loves to go diving. A highlight of this museum is that the owner/operator collected all the exhibits herself  from oceans all around the world  and the museum represents literally a lifetime of work and passion for the sea.Taking that into consideration  if you love to dive  and love the sea  this place is simply amazing  my girlfriend was absolutely in awe  snapping picture after picture and commenting on the rarity and difficulty of finding she'll after shell in such amazing condition. i went yesterday . this place was great. i really like it .and shop in the museum there are many art product.i bought one . good price and good design.i recomend this place.

I might not have the taste to appreciate the fine art  this is not a place for a young family. I agree that I am impressed by the collection of seashell  you can easily finish the tour in 30 mins. 6000won is a bit too much to pay.
I checked this place out based on the great reviews. While the seashell collection is impressive  6000 won was a bit steep for a place that takes about 15-20 minutes to check out.

For seashell lovers  this is a must visit museum with small entrance fee^^. They have the most exquisite collections of the world of seashells created into masterpieces of art collections. There are 2 storeys of them and a little cozy cafe on the ground floor to relax over a cup of coffee.

If not keep original sentence) With a collection of 7 800 species  hundreds of millions of beautiful shells and corals from all around the world joined by metal craft and copper  present the world's first 'Museum of Seashell Art'
Worth to visit  classy  fine art. This is an underrated destination  we do recommend it for adults looking for art and nature

At first  we thought this would just be a display of various seashells from around the world. But it was so much more than that! Just amazing and so artistic. This is more like a gallery of seashell and bronze art than a typical "museum". The artist has a brilliant eye for unique creations with seashells  making some of the installations really come to life. The staff were friendly and there is something to see at every turn (even the bathrooms!). Adult entrance fee: 6 000 won (approx. $5) and well worth it. You will not be disappointed with this museum! A wonderful surprise on our rainy day of touring.

It's one of the best small museums on Jeju island. I went there twice and each time spent couple of hours in sheer amazement and delight. Almost each sea shell installation strikes with its beauty. The bronze things are also interesting and sometimes funny. Check the bathroom  by the way :)There is much stuff in the gift shop but quite expensive. Small cafe is cozy arranged with bronze installations and green plants. Try tea and bagels  they are tasty.

This place is breathtakingly beautiful with especially kind staff. Every piece of art is a masterpiece. Nice (but expensive) giftshop and cute coffeeplace. Don't miss it if you are close by. I visited this place on the last day of a worktrip and it left a wonderful feeling about Jeju.
2nd time at jeju and 2nd time visiting this stadium  the building is huge! You can see it from far away. Worth the go
Really nice design for the stadium  volcano like. Brazil & Paraguay played here in 2002 FIFA WC. Close to the beach. Small but beautiful field.

Except if you're a soccer or stadium fanatic  I wouldn't make a huge detour to go there  but if you have some time and are in the vicinity  it can be interesting. The stadium itself isn't all that huge (35 000 seats)  but it's fairly modern and has a truly beautiful roof that looks like a canopy. There are things to do in the structure of the building (cinema  restaurants)  but make sure to actually get Inside the stadium  which you can do freely and was a pleasant surprise for me. I guess it would be nice to go there on a match day but I didn't have this opportunity.

I wouldn't go out of my way to see it but it is fun walking through the place. There are still some shops and a small waterpark/spa that only opens fully in the summer. Very quiet almost ghost town type of feel. Go karts are near by to if your into that

Have been to other football and the Olympic stadiums like the AC Milan one and those in Beijing  however  this one in Jeju is nothing. Firstly the signages are lousy. We followed the sign to the tour assembly but it turned out to be hall with different consignments and room vividly for the mainland Chinese tours.The stairs and inside the Sex Museum which is located on the second floor is dark and primitive. Interesting it was accessible by a stair in the middle of the carpark. But seeing the lightings as well as the Admission Fee notice printed on a torn A4 paper put on the window of the counter  we had no mood at all to enter into the museum.There is a spa land and other shops in the premises  but the signage is not updated  still indicating shops that were already closed. The stadium has become a low-class event hall instead of holding information and the class of a worldwide event. The only good thing about this site is that it is free. We entered onto the seating area without seeing any guard or staff  but we got very disappointed especially compared with the AC Milan museum and stadium.

Here was held the biggest event of the 2002 Korean and Japan Football World cup. The stadium blends in well with its surroundings  reminiscent of a small volcano in shape. The 6 pillars inside the ground represent the 6 continents.In rooms around the stadium  you can see memorabilia from the 2002 World Cup.Certainly worth a stop even if you're not a football fan.
The world cup stadium from 2002 is now the home of jeju united.Nice stadion with some shopping around. If you're in the area nice to see but not worth an extra trip.

Jeju World Cup Stadium is certainly worth stopping by if you are in the area. It looks superb from the outside and can be seen from a distance as you come down the hill from Seogwipo.Main entrance is open allowing you to walk in and spend some time in the stands for free. Tickets for Jeju United games are reasonably priced  and only attended up a small number of fans meaning they are up for grabs if you happen to time your visit in the K-League Classic season.Lots of busses pass by including the Airport Limo service (stop just in front) so pay a visit if you're a football fan or just want to see one of the 2002 World Cup's venues
Didn't take the tour but it's a cool stadium and can be combined with a film too at a decent cinema.. Popcorn was very sweet !

This stadium had an awesome design. I wouldn't travel far to see it but it was on the way so I popped it. I couldn't go inside so viewed from behind the gate. I can imagine watching a game their would be great

Never would have guessed but there's shopping  eating  a water park and movie theater at the world stadium. Jeju triathlon was headquartered here so I did that business. You can put on Hanboks (Korean clothing) and take pictures as well  that's all free.
Get a picture of the stadium from the highway. It looks like a ship sail:o) Its located right next to the beach and is great for photographers and anyone wanting to catch a soccer game!

While biking around Jeju Island my friend and I came across the world cup stadium. We took a short break and strolled around getting a good look at it. the stadium is of an interesting architectural design.
This is really a good size building for a small community. The large overhead is suspended by cable in a clear white fabric.An invitation to sport

Sports fans will probably enjoy this the most. Not really sure what to do here beyond appreciate the cool design for a couple of minutes and then go into the stadium for two more minutes. It's stunning  but likely best enjoyed during an actual game. The structure houses a sex museum (wasn't that interesting) and a paper doll museum (didn't try that one). Unless you're a soccer enthusiast or an architect  youll be fine enjoying its striking design as you drive by.

I strolled into the stadium primarily for my interest in sports. Unfortunately  during my stay on Jeju Island there were no games scheduled. The stadium is rather impressive and I would love to attend a major soccer game here.For any sports fan  stop by the stadium at the very least (15 minutes is sufficient). If you can buy tickets to a game  even better. Watching any Korean sporting event is an experience.

This place is massive! Truly a great venue to walk around. While it was closed the day I was there  I walked around the entire stadium and was impressed with everything outside of it. I went to the "Maze" next door and took the hot air balloon ride which gave me a great view of INSIDE the stadium! This place is gorgeous!
Yes! From far away it looks like a gigant clam!. No touring was available when we where there  but we parked near by and walked close and took pictures. It is huge  it is worth seeing!

The soccer games and cheap (6 000WON... about 6 USD) and the stadium is great. It was built for the World Cup in Korea in 2002. The schedules can be found online  just search Jeju United. You can bring your own food and drink (beer!). A great afternoon/night. Wear orange!

if you appreciate football games  this can be a memorable place for you to go. basically there's nothing much you can do there because the stadium gates are closed so you wont get to enter the stadium. But still  you can camwhoring around there and once you are done  maybe you can consider to go shopping at E-Mart which located just across the street from the stadium
We saw the World Cup Stadium at the start of Olle Trail 7-1. It was very impressive even though we could not enter the stadium. I'm glad we saw it!

The Stadium is closed almost all the week long except when a match is there  no visits are allowed inside  may be because that was in winter. The nice thing is that you can picture it from outside inside in  and a nearby small shops community & large e-Market place to shop & eat in their food-court. Nice play ground area around to check & may be to practice for free  you can see the local folks play around with some apparatuses  and machines to fit up
It is interesting place if you like soccer. Stadium is one of the the place were World Cup games took place. Karting experience is available near the stadium (25 000 W per adult; 15 minutes).
The architecture was beautiful. The stadium was opened to the public and you could enter the stands from one of the entrance beside a short exhibition on the world cup 2002.
Very modern and if you love soccer go see it. The outside of the building has 12 stone statues representing the soccer players who played here during the Olympics.

It's just a stadium with some architectural appeal but the shape tells a story  which is interesting. Try telling any football aficionado that it just a stadium and you will get howls of protest!From the 2002 FIFA World Cup it is designed around "the mouth of a volcano " and its roof in the shape of nets of traditional fishing boats in Jeju.So looking at it in that respect makes it more interesting.It was not open when we visited as of course there are no games here at the moment (although open during the summer months) so it was like looking into a fish bowl without the fish.Outside the stadium are many stone crafted 'dol hareubangs ' carved from porous basalt (volcanic rock).The statues' faces feature grinning expressions and bulging eyes without pupils  a long  broad nose  and slight smile and their hands rest on their bellies.These are quite common throughout Jeju and can be quite comic and a little suggestive!Have a peek here if in the area just to have at look at the stadium design and also the rock statues.Enjoy your visit!

Enter an oasis of watery fun  where 18 wave pools  rapids  spas and slides come together with six restaurants and a Korean-style jjimjilbang sauna to create Jeju's biggest indoor and outdoor water park. With baby nursing rooms  kids??pools  Asia's first double water slide  private cabanas  a variety of sauna rooms  hot snacks and fresh beer  there's something here for everyone in the family

The water park is ok. It would have been way better if you didn't have to pay extra for swim vests and extra for sun beds. So practically paying entrance fee doesn't mean you go and have fun. You are forced to spend good amount of money to have a good time.

Great  cosy  simple with a beautiful view  countryside atmosphere and the elegance of a modern coffee place. You can see how the plants grow and you can pet animals as well. A place to drink and eat something too.
My family visited Ilchul Land in a humid  scorching hot summer days. Michun Cave is the place you should visit and feel refreshed in summer.
It's well maintained and well organized. The Micheon cave is one of a kind with colorful nooks worthy of a snapshot.

Read that it was man- made garden !! After the visit I felt that this was one of the best Garden ever visited. The various plants and trees were really great and we spend a good 3 hrs walking round. The cave was wonderful ... even thou only 350m is open to public. Highly recommended even for adults .

This is a manmade park-like garden with a variety of plants and trees and water features. It is well worth the time it takes to walk through the grounds  just for the experience of viewing the bucolic setting. The main feature is Michon Cave which really didn't dazzle us as much as it apparently was supposed to. It's just a cave in which one walks down a slope to see some tacky lights and statues. The park  on the other hand  is scenic and pleasant. There are some concessions where they sell the usual tourist stuff.
Ilchul land is a man made garden with a cave. It is immaculately set up and looked after. I was quite happy that we visited and have seen what we saw.

We paid for our tickets and got past the entrance when it started pouring. We waited it out for maybe an hour or more  but it didn't stop  only got harder. The lady at the ice cream shop must have felt sorry for us because she gave us chairs to sit on while we waited and even some free chocolates. We asked the ticket counter if we can get a refund since we didn't actually see anything except for the sign  but unfortunately they said no. It seemed like it would have a been a great place if we actually got to go past the front hahaha! At least they made a lot of money selling umbrellas that day.

The place is essentially a large botanical garden and cave in one attraction.First  botanical garden is quite large and can take quite a while to walk. The grounds are nicely manicured  with many plants  flowers  and trees. There are also some water fountains and small man made falls. There are also some statues and other stone objects in the park. There is also a greenhouse with various desert plants. It certainly isn't something you really need to see  but it is a pleasant walk through the area.However  the main attraction is Micheon cave. It is probably a naturally occurring cave. Nonetheless  the cave's ground has been leveled artifically to make it easy to walk on - compared to Manjanggul Cave which has a very uneven and dangerous floor. There is really not too much to see in the cave other than feel how cool it is and a few weird looking large figurines of cavemen...
You have to go down and see this tunnels   it can be this one or any other on the island. There are also very nice gardensa and statues at this site

We went to Ilchul Land primarily for Micheon cave. For families and those with small children this cave is great. We even saw some strollers making there way in the dark. We went in July and while it was hot and humid outside  inside the cave we needed light jackets - the difference in temperature was that drastic. The kids walked down and immediately asked for their sweaters. That said  the temperature change was welcome on such a hot summer day. The cave is not very long which is great for kids  it's fairly well lit while maintaining the dark atmosphere of an underground cave. It's wet inside  like most caves are so be sure to have some good shoes on and the part open to the public is quite large with some parts requiring you to duck (clearance for a short section is 1.5 meters).Apart from the cave the other attractions are good if you're looking for a leisurely stroll with things to see. The park is set up so that you follow a blue line on the ground that takes you through all the different parts of Ilchul Land. There were a number of sculptures  some gardens  Jeju stone men  and artwork. The cactus garden was hot and interesting. Not many "activities" on the walk but a good stroll. I forget the exact admission price but I believe it was about ??0000 per adult and ??000 per child.
Goin on summer  like another park  but the cave lil bit creepy  and i dont know feel very cold even its on summer. No guide in cave  and creepy.

We went in Jun and there were hardly any flowers. Mainly statues. Nothing much in the cave. Just like a normal park with a small man-made waterfall. Entrance fees not cheap  too. Don't waste your time !

These caves are quite common all around the island  and this one is a well maintained and easily accessible example. Be aware though that if its been raining the day before you are likely to be dripped upon  but it's tolerable. Also  depending on the time of year  you will probably want to wrap up warm as it can be quite fesh inside.

This place is pretty new I believe  it wasn't built 3 years ago when I visited. It was a very enjoyable walk around  the place is pretty huge and in some areas  construction hadn't finished yet. It's basically a really huge garden  lots of really pretty flowers and areas to take photos of. And I believe there are some animal enclosures somewhere in the middle of the park too. Our guide recommended visiting this place and the cave they had here  saying that it was all better than Hallim Park. Though I personally preferred Hallim Park. I found the cave here to be pretty creepy and really dark  best to skip over if you aren't into caves. There's nothing much to see in the cave anyway.
Nice walk through with lots of photo chances. All the descriptions were in korean but still was nice. The cave was nice and i liked it was self guided. The cactus display is worth visiting.

Located on the eastern part of Jeju lies Ilchul Land  a cultural spot that showcases Jeju's ecology which consists of the Micheon Cave  Subyeon Park  Folk Village  Wild Flower Bonsai Garden  and Cactus Greenhouse etc??For fans of Running Man (?°ë‹ë§?  this is one place to visit as the team actually filmed here before: various signboards showcasing certain place scenes (at certain corners) that occurred during the filming of Running Man; bringing you a step closer to your favorite Running Man characters! The first stop was Micheon Cave  a cave that is a designated Natural Monument and one of the representative lava tubes of Jeju. Within this cave lie beautifully landscaped and manicured gardens which include a pond (Chumsung Dae).After we were done with the Micheon Cave  it was off to visit the Folk Village with a little yummy ice-cream of a snack on the way. The village was a replica of what would have been in the past with a millstone and buildings with commentary. There were even ?˜live??black pigs which were as long as my golden retriever! *Black pork is apparently a famous product of Jeju.For more on my experience and photos  please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/ilchul-land-micheon-cave-folk-village.html

If you are big fan of the Korean variety show Running Man (?°ë‹ë§?  you will enjoy walking around Ilchul Land. Serious fans (like myself) will remember that the cast visited this attraction in 2012  episode 89  featuring the Alice in Wonderland theme. Ilchul Land is quick to play up on the connection for fans as there are various signboards placed around the attraction showing you exactly where certain scenes took place. Great for taking photos to show that you have been there!For regular visitors/tourists  Ilchul Land is more of like a very well maintained outdoor park  with lush and verdant landscaped scenery including bonsai plants  palm trees and even miniature waterfalls. However  the highlight for me was the natural underground cave/tunnel  which you can explore - do go all the way to the end (until you reach the roped off area) and mind your head as it is a bit low in parts. There are some carvings and statues placed inside the caves  whereas I would have preferred that it was left in its natural state. If I remember correctly  it was about a 10mins stroll all the way in. Other areas of interest within Ilchul Land would be the mock-up of a Korean village where you can see the famous Jeju black pig.All in all  you can probably spend about an hour at this attraction or less if you do a quick run through.
