The Joanne Bear Museum is one of the stops in the package tour that we availed of. It is basically a collection of stuffed bears that Joanne Oh has created  each bear hand made. There are three buildings where all the bears are housed. We were there in winter and the place was well-heated. The pathway between the buildings were open air  though. The bears came in different sizes  colors and variations. There are some depict historical or cultural scenes  others depict pop culture. The bears are all finely crafted. Unfortunately though  many of the signage are in Korean only.There are several displays where guests can pose with the bears. One of those bears  a polar bear  was featured in a Korean drama  ?œParadise Ranch.??I especially loved the displays that feature the acronym of the place (JB) because it is my initial as well. There is a souvenir shop which sell?”you guessed it right?”stuffed bears. I wanted to have one as a souvenir so I was settling for the least expensive keychain bear when I saw a much larger 8-inch plushie being sold at a discounted rate; it was only 2 000 won more expensive than the keychain so I got it instead. As with many of the Joanne bears  it an embroidery of Joanne Oh's signature.
A must go place for Bear lovers? A non bear lover also love and enjoy this place too ?™ˆ Planned to visit teddy bear museum at Seoul; spontaneous change to Jeju teddy bear Museum~
This is a good place to spend some time. I really love the Obama bear. It looks so cute! and also the ones with Korean traditional clothes. Joanna is really obsessed wtih teddy bears!!

It takes entrance fee to enter the museum  but that's okay as there are three venues in total. With lots of different appearances bears  such as dressing up like students and wedding. The most memorial teddy bear is the president Obama  it is similar to the real Obama but in bear form. The top floor of the second venue is about wedding and relationships between lovers  so it is a great place for lovers to take pictures and have memories with the teddy bear couples. Although I am not a teddy bear fan  I took lots of photos in that first two venues. And in the third venue  bears are for sell  so please remember not to photo bears in the third venue as it is subjected to copy right. Finally  my father bought me a bear which I think is the cutest as a present of graduation. It takes about 40k-80k unequally per bear  but I think it is valuable as all bears are made in Jeju.So  if you think you don't have any way to spend your money  you can go to this teddy bear museum and buy your favorite bear as an emblem of stepping on Jeju.

This is not exactly a museum  but a shop impersonating as museum  that sells teddy bear. Uses gimmick of hand make teddy bear that resembled Obama and some other celebrities  but really nothing interest unless one is crazy over teddy bear.

It's a teddy bear collector's dream to come here. Joanne Bear Museum have higher quality bears compared to the other bear museum in Jeju Island (which I forgotten the name). The beginning of the trip is a exhibition of teddy bears with theme clothing  which is very adorable! At the end of the trip  you can own one of the teddy bears there. Note that it's quite pricey  but the quality is there and it's said that it used organic material to make it.

As far as I know there are two bear museums on Jeju Island. One is the Teddy Bear Museum while the other is the Joanne Bear Museum. My aunt decided to go to the Joanne Bear Museum due to her friends' recommendations. It was the best decision she has made for that Korea trip. I wasn't a fan of teddy bears but I was surprised and overwhelmed by all bears  coming in different colours and sizes. It's even more special because every bear in the Joanne Bear Museum is handmade.Furthermore  the decorations in the Joanne Bear Museum are very interesting too. I have never seen such decorations  using bears to enhance the decorations. I will definitely come back for a second trip!

Pyoseon Beach might not be the most picturesque beach in Jeju but it's vast and didn't feel that crowded even in the middle of the high season. Because of the large sand area exposed during low tides  it can be quite the hike to the water then. But the low depth of the water and the large sand area makes it a good beach for children. As with most other popular Jeju beaches  there is a good selection of restaurants nearby.
Very peaceful and quiet. Hardly see any cars around. Very nice place to stroll and chill by the beach. Few cafes along the beach
One of the many pretty beaches around the island  this one not so crowded  so a big plus for that. Very nice.

This is a circular beach that turns into a lake on the rising tide  then dries again on the ebbing tide. m The water is not too deep (about a meter) and the half moon shaped beach is one of the largest in Jeju. The sand is particularly delicate and soft on the feet. The stone sculptures are worth a viewing too. Lots of things to do nearby  Folklore Village  Namwon Keunang and Seopjikoji. Loads of free parking close by.

Just over the road from the Jeju Folk Village  the area has some lovely sandy areas to play around; cool memorial area of the women divers of Jeju and several snack shops (a little expensive). Toilets available and some very nice views. Worth a quick visit when in the area.

We come here for the lighthouse where Korean drama Iris was filmed. The view is exceptional and didn't disappointed. One unexpected experience is we got to see the women divers. They caught bunch of sea urchins and see their male partners cut it. I wish we could taste it but seeing it is good enough.

Pyoseon Beach is just the opposite of Jeju Folk Village.So after visited the Village  we came here.The beach is pretty large with wide white sands.It is the perfect place for families to spend some time relaxing  particularly at low tide with its lake-like pools.It has abundant parking space  public toilet (with shower) and cam-ground around the square.Near the beach  there is white lighthouse near the shore.This lighthouse is where the last scene in Kdrama Iris (2009) was film.

Haha worst museum i have ever visited. For non-Korean speakers  95% of the displays are in Hangul  ?œê?. The museum is comprised of 3-4 large rooms of tacky semi-chocolate related items  the chcolate displayed is random chocolate primarily bought from Korean supermarkets... some are just empty boxes. The owner seems to be a Liverpool F.C. fan and for some odd reason there was a compilation of Gerrard goals and a signed England shirt; easily the best part.

The chocolate museum was a highlight of our Jeju trip in 2020  the fresh chocolate made by the resident chocolatier is a real treat. Be aware that not only the quality  but also the price of the chocolate is on an international level  with a decent-sized box going for some 30 dollars. But for buying three boxes  we got three tickets for a chocolate making workshop  which was greatly enjoyed by the kids.We will come again  if only to get some memorable treats. The museum itself is informative  but don't expect too much.

Total waste of money (6000 for adults). Tragically outdated  tacky  uninteresting. Not much focus on actual chocolate - we were expecting samples  exciting cafe  lots of choice to buy from. There is none of this. Shop super overpriced. Don't waste your time.
I wanted to rip my eyes out. Don't waste your time. It also smells like faeces because of the pork factory next door.

We just visited the chocolate museum as a family and it was a bit of a let down. The tickets were 6000 for adults (tickets for children in elementary I think were 4500?) and they gave us free Americano. There really wasn't that much to see  and the place smelled funny. I think if you?™re really interested in learning about the past of cacao and chocolate in Korea then this might be a fun place to visit  but if you don't have much interest in that  it might be a waste of money.However they do offer chocolate making classes every hour for little kids under 13. So there were a lot of children there when we went. Might be a fun place to visit with children :)They also sell chocolate  and we tried a sample and it was pretty good and rich in quality. We also bought 3 bars of 70% cacao for 30 000. The original price was 36 000  but with the entree ticket you get a 6 000 discount.

Unfortunately the place described on the web sight was not to be seen. From the outside you have high hopes but once you enter you see that it is in disrepair and that the chocolate samples and even to purchase chocolate is not to be found and then over priced at best. When you buy your ticket the expected hot chocolate is a terrible cup of coffee. It's really unfortunate because by going through it  you can see its potential but sadly it's just not there.

This museum is not the easiest to find  located in an industrial type area. Upon entrance you receive a free sample of chocolate and a hot chocolate (not sure if this was offered due to the chilly  rainy weather  but it was definitely appreciated). Some interesting finds from around the world  historical facts  and treasures. There is an area where you may observe chocolate pieces being made for sale in the adjacent gift shop. Good stop for a rainy day on Jeju Island. Gift shop is a little pricey. Teenaged daughter loved it; teenaged son was bored.

Just a museum  you will read a lot of stuffs about chocolate history and process of making. First I thought everything inside the house made of chocolate  but you don't expect that for a cheap entrance fee. One of the highlight is the workshop  if you are planning to attend with your kids  better check the timing. We bought some souvenir too and their chocolate are great. I didn't give a higher rating due to following... 1.) They provide free drink  but it is a coffee  I think it would be nice if its a chocolate drink 2.) Some interesting areas (Cocoa garden and kitchen) are not accessible when we visit (not sure if there is a special arrangement for it). Overall  it is not that scam and most likely I will visit it again when I'm with the kids.

Just your run of the mill chocolate "factory" museum. They have all the info about the Cacao bean and how to make chocolate  a gift shop to buy chocolate  and that's it. They have a little chocolate workshop for kids. And kids only which was kind of disappointing.It's great if you have kids but if you are going to just to go or with your boy/girlfriend or spouse I wouldn't. It's mediocre and offers the same info about chocolate you could learn by googling it.

It's 3000won for adults and 2000won for kids. They give you a gift voucher equivalent to the entrance fee which you can use to offset purchases or the DIY chocolate making session (12 000won). You get a box of 10 chocolates at the end of the 15 min session. You have to wait another 15 min for chocolates to solidify. Other than the DIY session  there's really nothing worth looking at here.

Visited during a rainy day. Really not much to see but a large shop for purchasing chocolate with displays of chocolate from around the world. Lots of locally produced chocolate to purchase. It put in a half hour during the rain

When I was planning my trip to Jeju  I found this museum has got half positive and half negative comments from travelers. Well ??I decided to have a look by myself. When our car got near to the place  there was a strong smell. I was then told that there is a piggery farm nearby which stinks out the whole place. The ticket was not cheap but it included a cup of coffee plus a discount in the shop. The appearance of the building is interesting with an open courtyard. The first impression was not so bad.However when I got inside  it was quite disappointing. I think the management should consider a renovation  or at least a deep cleaning and some maintenance. I just felt I was in a dusty old weird mansion. Maybe those exhibits are precious and rare  but they are not well presented. For example  they put lots of chocolate boxes from all over the world in the same window display without proper descriptions. How can the people think that those boxes are precious when they are packed in a glass cabinet? The lighting on the second floor was horrible. The rooms were so dark adding horrific ambiance to the museum.

We only went because it was raining and we needed some indoor attractions. We needed to occupy our young children (ages 9 and 4) so we decided to take a trip to the museum. It was much smaller than we had anticipated. Friendly staff who allowed us to trip some of the more unusual chocolates before we purchased them. We did find the same chocolates at E-Mart that was less expensive. The kids liked the chocolate school but we thought the kit was a bit overpriced as you could do the same thing in your kitchen.
If you're in the area  check it out. It costs 4 000 Won to get in but they give you a coupon worth 3 000 Won to use in the gift shop.

It's too far to make it worth your time. Suggest to skip and go to chocolate museums in Belgium or Germany  which are much much better. This doesn't cut it and exhibits feel a little neglected....The chocolates on sale are very expensive too. But I think the locals may find it an educational intro of chocolate for their children...

Went to visit this attraction even though I saw some negative reviews as I have planned some attractions based on region and this is some thing that I think the kids would love to visit.Entrance fee is pricey at $5k won as there is practicably nothing much to see and do inside. After buying the tickets  the staff would give the adults coffee and kids chocolates. The display were very old  like it has been there for 3 or 4 decades and we felt uneasy as it looks dirty. There is a kitchen whereby apprentice showcase their skils on chocolate making. Wanted to buy some chocolates since we are there. But they dont seemed to be interested as the minimum sale item cost about $39k for a box of chocolates. Not worth my moneh and thus left empty handed. Adults ans children were disappointed.

Entrance fee of KRW5 000 per adult which includes a huge cup of hot black coffee (I don't drink coffee and couldn't change it for a hot chocolate drink). The museum is located on one floor with various displays. Towards one end there's a glass concept kitchen where the various chocolates are made and a little further down  the chocolate shop. A box of 8-12 pieces could cost upwards of KRW13 000  and the lady was kind enough to let us try a dark chocolate which ended up quite yummy (not too sweet nor bitter  think it was a 60 or 70% one).

I do not like they indirectly force a visitor to buy their entrance ticket to the souvenir shop though the entrance ticket after that can get discount when you purchase any chocolate. It is small  but can experience in making chocolate or macaron. Their sample chocolate got black chocolate and white chocolate mixed together but in fact the class provide one color of chocolate to each participant. Thus  we cannot mix the color together as we got one color only. Overall  is normal place without any surprise for us. But there is a nearby local restaurant selling local food (abalone bimbap and etc) providing baby chair which I truly appreciate it.
Full of Chocolates for you to taste and buy. You can join the chocolate making class too with your family.
The admission is cheap but boring. There is a chocolate making class but  I didn't do it. It was filled with kids.

We regretted going to this place. The entrance fee is 5 000 won and they give you a 3 000 coupon to use when you buy their products. There is nothing to see except display of chocolates from different countries which is available at a supermarket. Really it is a waste of money and waste of time.

It is the worst place we have visited in whole Korea. The introduction of chocolate production is tiny and mostly in Korean only. We learned that Leibniz is a company of Russia and Kinder chocolate is coming from Asia. So it is not only tiny it has a lot of wrong information as well. After 10 minutes we have seen everything and left again.

This is not a bias assessment. I would be glad if the establishment owner would take in advise from visitor feedback. This is my first time to rate an establishment with such a low rating. It is a total rip-off as entrance fee is collected before cafe and store. There nothing impressive with the collection and exhibit area is extremely small. There is another fees impose for DIY chocolate making session. No educational value  no entertainment value. I would not recommend it to anyone.

for 6000won per a ticket for an adult  what you get is a coupon worthy of 3000won which u can use to buy chocolate at the shop...I still remember the first thing that the ticket officer told me was ... I could use the coupon to buy chocolate at the shop located at basement.What I feel so disappointed is that the so-called showroom only displays chocolates made in different shapes or figures. Also  what I can buy from the basement was chocolates from other countries. No Jeju features at all for both chocolates and display.This shop is a total disgrace to Korea.

That is the first time I am rating a place terrible. To begin with there are only Korean introduction and description for all the items and collections displayed there. We all read Korean don't we?As stated in other reviews this place has zero content. I can easily find more chocolate related stuff in a convenience store that this so called chocolate land. Worse  the entry ticket is bundled with a purchase voucher of the chocolate items sold at the store in this place. Contradictory to the all Korean introductions and descriptions  the chocolate available in the store are all international brands. If you are looking for the experience of travelling to Korea to buy chocolate probably from your own country  there you go!
This is the most boring museum ever. They have some stuff made with chocolate but it's nothing nice. Also if you want to take the chocolate class you have to pay more.

It was located behind the mbc k-pop. The place was quite deserted. Nothing much to see.. you are given ??000 voucher each for a ??000 admission fee. Literally  this place is just encouraging you to shop at their shop.

There aren't a lot of stuff you can do here unless you join the chocolate making class which costs around 20 000won including the kit. The good thing is that the entry fee (3 000 won) may be used to purchase anything here. There's a small shop that sells ice cream here so it's a good place to rest.
Have choclate variety.Price is 3 000 for adult and 2 000 for childs.Choclate lab is amazing you can make choclate box by yourself.

As the Chocolate Land is within 10 minutes??walk from the Teddy Bear Museum in the Jungmun Resort area ??just follow the direction on the sign-posts ??my family and I had no hesitation to visit it on a rainy Sunday.Getting there and fees: First and foremost  you have to note that Chocolate Land is different from Chocolate Museum. Chocolate Land is in the south central part of Jeju while Chocolate Museum is in the south west Jeju. We didn't need the GPS coordinate/code for Chocolate Land but it's 7381197 for anyone who's driving there directly. The entrance fee for adults is 3000 won and 2000 won for children. A voucher was given back for every purchased ticket which can be redeemed at the gift shop or the cafÃ© or the Chocolate School.The Museum/Attraction: After going past the ticketing counter  you then turn right. The section on the left is a cafÃ© and photograph/selfie stops of different types of Korean houses and benches with toy bears. There's even a figurine of Santa Claus in front of one house  which was interesting considering Christmas is still some 6 months away. The section on the right is the exhibits on the history of chocolates  with the words written only in Korean. We went down the stairways to the level below in which there's a Chocolate School which teaches chocolate making at 120 000 won with lessons starting every hour from 10am to 6pm (I think the children would be more interested than adults). We didn't go into the School; instead  we walked past M&M figurines and a Christmas tree (again interesting) and reached the chocolate shop where there are interesting exhibits of chocolates (behind glass) from America  Europe and Asia. The gift shop has an extensive selection of chocolates (I think slightly more than outside). The prices of the Jeju chocolates of the same brand at the gift shop were slightly more expensive compared to those selling outside Chocolate Land. However  the Chocolate Land chocolates became slightly cheaper than those outside when we utilised the discount vouchers. Unique local Jeju chocolates are those with pink cactus flowers  mandarin oranges and hallabong fillings. We couldn't wait till Christmas?¦we ate some of the chocolates before we left Jeju  and these were yummy!There is a small observation area (Chocolate Garden) outside the building where the view looks towards the sea. There's also a statue of Willy Wonka from the 1971 movie ?˜Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory??where you could take a photograph and selfie with. But we couldn't go outside because it's raining.I recommend visiting the Chocolate Land if you have the time and if you have an appreciation of chocolates. Otherwise  I think you wouldn't miss much if you decide to skip it.
The only value here I think is let the kids make their own chocolates. It's a funny experience. Apart from that  the display is a joke. Anyway  the entrance fee is low and it doesn't matter much.
Cafe didn't have a Cafe Mocha?! Just chocolates inside museum boxes. If you don't have kids  skip it! If you go then the kids will enjoy the chocolate making...
Interesting to see historic chocolate packaging  however  amount  quality and selection of display have reflected on cost of admission fee.Great souvenir shop in the basement!

Museum is the wrong term for this facility. It is more of a showcase of chocolate that the owners children may have learned to make. You pay 3000won per person which you technically "get back" if you purchase their price gouged chocolates or do their make your own chocolate class for 12  000 won more. Save yourself the pain and buy some snickers and M&M's at the close by 7-11 instead.

It was a good experience to make chocolates with my family. Especially  my princesses really enjoyed it ! Pictures painted by chocolate was impressive to me !Overall  I strongly recommend to families with young kids as the process was simple and safe.

First you pay a 3 000 won entrance fee  which you can use to get a discount if you decide to buy any of their ridiculously overpriced chocolate. The "museum" is just a bunch of boxes and chocolate from some places around the world. That's all there is. The only other thing to do is make chocolate. You have to pay 12 000 won for that  2 000 more if you want other colors like white or pink chocolate. So in summary  you pay 3 000 to get in so that you can pay more to make chocolate. If you skip this attraction  you wouldn't be missing much and saving yourself some money.

The chocolates there are not exactly cheap. We found cheaper ones on sale by the tourist attractions. Not exactly worth paying 3 000won to see some choco display. Nothing really that impressive too. The 3 000 won entrance ticket can be used to redeem for drinks or offset chocolate purchases within the museum too.

Calling this place a museum is absolute fraud. The entrance fee is 3000 won which is returned to you in the form of a coupon for the cafe or gift shop - both of which are insanely overpriced. The 'displays' are ridiculous - chocolate gold coins  chocolate Easter eggs  Guylian seashell-shaped chocolates  posters of the film 'Chocolat ' a statue of Willy Wonka. It's almost as if the museum is teasing the West for its chocolate traditions - if it can even be called that. There is really nothing of interest in this museum. There is  however  a pretty nice view of the ocean to the rear of the museum.

The building is attached to the "jeju tourism" board (or something like that). It costs about 4 or 5 000 won to get in  then handed a coupon for a discount at the cafe or any of the products. The children enjoyed it as they got to make chocolate for 10 000 which included a take home mold. The museum isn't much to look at but just enough to make your mouth water. It is close enough to all the other activities in the area  if traveling with kids  this is a good "trade off" point to let them have some fun.

First  there is nothing worth seeing in this place. The exhibits were not even interesting-think chocolates shaped after teddy bears and placed in display cabinets. Their ultimate objective is to lure you to their shop which sells chocolate that....can be bought all over Jeju island. They don't even make their own chocolate.Second  they are liars. The saleswoman introduced the jeju orange chocolates to me  gave me a sample to try and recommended the "best" tasting brand. I tried it and i did like it. She recommended getting the set of 5 small boxes (each box containing 8 pieces of chocolates) because it was more worth it than the bigger box which was going for the same price but had 2 pieces less. I bought the set of 5 small boxes. When I got back  i tried the chocolates. Guess what? They tasted like cheap imitation chocolates. Nothing like the sample she gave me. Worse  each box only had a MAXIMUM<- note  of 6 pieces of chocolates. In addition  the saleswoman had such a bad attitude after I said i would only get one set of 5 small boxes. This place is totally not worth the trip. You can get better chocolates even at the airport  at a cheaper price. Don't waste your time and money.?¬?

There wasn't much to look and read (all in Korean) but caring and friendly staff made our day.For one of the most visited city or area for foreign tourists  it's hard to believe that the most of the places do not have English speaking staff.We were having hard time finding good place to go and dine  recommendations by the staff at the Chocolate Land were very very helpful. Also  the chocolates we purchased with his help turned out very good.If you are in Jung Moon tour sector  need a little break for a free coffee (it's free with a coupon you get when you pay an admission) and some help from an English and Chinese speaking staffs.

It's 3000 Won to enter and it is mostly just a chocolate shop. They do chocolate making classes  if you are interested  but that costs an additional 10 000 - 12 000 won (sorry  I am not sure about the exact price. We asked  but I don't remember). You can use your entrance fee to purchase chocolate  but way not just buy chocolate somewhere else?
There is no chocolate model  just Chocolate shop  don't think to go there. its poorest chocolate museum in the world.

We already know its gonna rain the whole day based on the weather forecast that's why we were in this area as it is full of museum...So... We run into this Choc Land after visiting the 'believe it or not museum' & teddy bear museum. Ermm  how to say  you can use part of the entrance ticket to buy chocolate here  and there were many cute & special chocolate displayed... But  that was it  no more no less. So... Unless you don't mind  you may dropby to buy some chocolate & snap some nice picture  rest a bit as there is not much people here. Else you may wanna consider stay longer in the Believe it or not Museum or even the Alive Museum :)

It is hard to say anything good about this place. Basically  it is a small chocolate gift shop that charges $3 a person to enter. You receive a coupon good for $3 back on any purchase. I suppose it is their way to ensure that you buy something.The only interesting thing was that they had these cookie balls that you smashed with a hammer to eat.

What WERE they thinking of! The "museum" is a few glass cases with examples of bars/boxes of chocolates. The "factory" is a table where you can buy cooking chocolate and make your own. The only good news is that your (HUGE) entrance fee is refunded in the way of a coupon to use at the (VERY OVERPRICED) chocolate shop. There is NOTHING here. It's AWFUL.Buy your choccies in the supermarket and give this place a wide berth.
Visited it today but nothing interesting except for some chocolate goodies for sales. Rather disappointed to be honest.

Very disappointing. There were a few panels in the entrance hall that had information about chocolate and very poorly kept display boxes  but everything was only in Korean. Downstairs  you can see chocolate packages from different countries  but mostly ordinary products that can be bought in Korean supermarkets. No effort was given to make a proper display with special chocolates. Plus  some chocolates were mislabeled under the wrong countries. There was a station where chocolates in bags could be squeezed into molds. I was not able to participate because the staff panicked when they saw a non-Korean face  despite the fact that I spoke Korean to them. Do yourself a favor and go in the convenience store across the road - there is a better display of chocolate there.

Indeed a disappointing experience. Yes  this is just an excuse to get you to the gift shop  but at least they could have made the trip there interesting. The story of chocolate is among the most fascinating in the histories of commodities  but they made it a torture. You will see some exhibits on the history of chocolate  a few displays of old boxes and cases of chocolates  and some needless toy sculptures  but mostly a forgettable experience. You do have to pay a small amount and get a coupon for your chocolate or drink purchase. So  if you are desperate to eat some chocolate  or it's raining heavily outside  or you need quickly some air-conditioning  then give it a try; otherwise  enjoy Jeju's natural scenery and wonders instead.

If you want to see a bunch of boxes of chocolate from all over the world  this is the place for you. The 3000 won you pay to enter gives you a discount to what you can buy there so if you want to buy chocolate you won't feel ripped off  but you can buy the same chocolate in any gift shop for the same price. There are a lot of great places on Jeju. I wouldn't go out of your way to visit here.

Chocolate land  is an interesting place to visit  it is close to Teddy Bear museum  they charge 3000 won for enterance  & give you coupon for the same amount  so when you buy chocolates the amount is deducted. It consists of 2 floors  the lower level has workshop where I saw people experimenting with chocolates  I did not because the did not know english.They have exhibition where chocolates from all parts of the world shown.They have samples on both levels to taste & then decide which flavor to buy. The upper level has cubicles with history of chocolates  & nice statues made of chocolates.The upper level has coffee shop where you can rest & have hot or cold drinks  icecream & chocolates.

Located 100m from Boo Young Hotel  you can just walk up. It;s a 5 level building slightly similar to HKCC in Wan Chai. There is a 7-11 convenient store but closes early. In house also a buffet restaurant  a bank and a Duty Free Supermarket where you have to pick up the perfumes  liquors and cigarettes at airport.
It is big and really fun to hang  people come here with business  so not much to review. It is pretty cool.

This is a crown jewel for Jeju Island. Plenty of facilities and convention area. When I was there  a radiology convention packed the Center. A little bonus is a place where you can buy duty free items outside of the airport. Very convenient.

It is not tourist attraction but great place for a conference  inside you have seven eleven and gift shop - I would advice this gift shop with nice sweets  tangerines and black garlic. Tangerines are the best from this Island!
A nice and very big convention center with some shops and a very good restaurant which we visited. If you are around take visit. Not a must.

the facilities are excellent  very spacious  and comfortable. staff great. out on it own with little to attract you and but great facility. not sure who supplied the food first night plenty to eat second night they ran out. end of our evenings there was no where to book/order a cab so thank goodness the BooYung hotel assisted.

I participated in an event focusing on renewable energy and green growth at this superb convention centre. It is modern with meeting rooms upstairs having amazing almost panoramic view of the Jeju coastline. It has large exhibition floor  with large conference rooms on the three floors  but also bilateral meetings rooms that are convenient and centrally located. The catering and banquets were simply exquisite with great Korean cuisine and the banquet room and service were just incredible. I found it very convenient place for participating and networking.

Drove by the convention center in jeju on our day tour in November 2016. Located near the jungmann cliffs. There are some restaurants which are a 5 minute drive away. Lots of windows in the building. Also  many palm trees adorn the grounds surrounding the convention center. Our guide said it was a fairly new building in jeju.
From  this convention center  we could see the Hyatt and beautiful sea of Jeju. I heard this place has duty free shop but we didn't go inside the building.
Located south of the island  in front of the see  easily accessible with the airport shuttle limousine. Plenty of space for organizing major events.

The architecture of this conference centre is the first exciting and majestic comment on the centre. It has big conference rooms with the best facilities to host big events. I attended the international mercury conference here and the logistics of the venue provided us with a flawless event. There are also several fast food restaurants at the bottom level of the centre  with a duty free shop on the other side. It is a local attraction and the visitors seem to enjoy it too  since it was constantly busy. On the second floor is a curio shop for some gifts from Jeju.The airport limousine bus no 600 stops outside entrance of the venue  but there are local taxis frequently available to take you anywhere.

It is a must see place for a tourist to visit the area near to the convention center especially place near to the beach at the back side of convention center. The beach area with loan provide a haven like feeling for those who love peace. After being travelled around Jeju that place held at the top place among other places.
The view from the bridge is really pretty but we wanted to see the fall and you could barely see it because it was so far away.
In my opinion it's much more beautiful and interesting from outside than on the bridge.Of course better to visit in good weather condition :)

We walked over the bridge to get to Cheonjeyeon Falls. I didn't think too much of it. When we were below the bridge level and I looked up  I was very pleasantly surprised by the beautiful dragon motifs on the side of the bridge.

Was there during winter  thus not much water can be seen under the bridge. Can see far away on the bridge  and the view was nice. Other than that  nothing much at the attraction. There was one fountain of various animals heads  and supposedly you are to face any one of them to throw in a coin and make a wish according to what you wanted.

I thought my travel period was not very ideal. In end Nov  I had expected to miss the autumn foliage  and yet too early for snow.Jeju (particularly the park surrounding Seonim Bridge) surprised me. There were still some red and yellow leaves on the trees. Not a lot  I admit... but sufficiently beautiful.I didn't really fancy the intricate design of the bridge. But loved the stroll in the park as it felt relaxing and tranquil.
I would recommend to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and walk outside the park for better view of the bridge. Well built. Very clean beautiful park and falls.
This is one of the beautiful bridges I?™ve ever seen so far. The sceneries are breathtaking the air is so fresh and surrounding are greens

It was windy and cold the time I visit which was 1st of March 2018  this place was made famous by the Korean drama "All in " many years ago   scenery was so so only . The all in church turn into a candy house .
When we go the weather is not on our side. Lot of mist and can't see clearly from TOP. Bt it would be better if clear sky.

There is a long steep path in order to reach the lighthouse on top. But that shouldn't be a problem as the scenery along the road is empowering your feet to work. In the middle of the path  there is a candy house like building. But unfortunately  it was reconstructing at that moment. So  I bought a chocolate ice cream beside the reconstruction to settle my unhappiness. The ice cream tastes unexpectedly good  it is rich in chocolate and smooth when I put it into my mouth. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the lighthouse  we took several pictures there  but no one is perfectly taken because of strong wind  our hair flowing like crazy  so we didn't spend much time on the lighthouse.We took about 30 minutes there and didn't have a chance to visit the building at that time  so I strongly recommend you to go there at autumn or spring and plan more than half an hour if you are deciding to visit there.

The outlook has been dressed up and over designed. It looks like a candy house rather than a church. It is quite disappointed especially when you have been walking from a long way out there in order to move closer to it but it does not give you any romantic feeling at all.
Walking along the coastal and climb up to the lighthouse is not a bad idea. Horse riding course nearby. Relaxing and enjoyed the cool wind blow .

There is a big signage in Korean at the entrance next to the ticketing booth which we didn't apprehend  but the window of the ticketing booth was blocked with wood and when we moved to the back of the premises  we found back doors not closed and things which seemed to be exhibits were scattered on the backyard.

how lucky we are can reach this place at perfect time  a good weather and sunset. Enjoy every single of the land  peaceful. If I have more times I will stay here for couples day.The park was pretty enough  for couple or family  kids will fun here. they can ride horse or just running around the garden. very recommended to visit.
i didn't go into the house but only walked along the path outside. the sea view is beautiful and you can plan to go with some other attractions nearby

To reach the place  need to walk along not properly paved route with long bushes  initially thought the guide had taken us to wrong place. Quiet place with nice coastal view. Unfortunately  we didn't manage to go to the church as there's sudden downpour  left us no choice but to end the visit. I saw horse carriage and shuttle bus service that can bring you around.

I decided to visit this place after reading some good reviews and was not disappointed. The coastal view is breathtaking and breathing in the sea breeze was relaxing. Other than the church nothing much else to see  but you can take some nice pictures here. Seongsan Sunrise peak is nearby so don't miss that too. Tried the barbecued cuttlefish that they were selling there and it was fresh and delicious.

We spent a half day here for a short walk. It was such a peaceful and relaxing place. You could see many coastal rocks and Udo. If you like  you could ride a horse to wander a while. You may also visit the lighthouse and the chapel nearby. This was one of must go tourist points in Jeju!

Nothing much to do over there. You will only walk walk walk to look at the view. With the cooling wind and nice view. I made me feel very relax and the walk is enjoyable. I think it is a must visit place if you have not been here before.
The view around the curch is really nice. I didn't go inside the church.The location near seongsan ilchubong.Make sure u visit two of them when u come to jeju
The house and church were korean drama set. It's easy to reach from parking lot and the scenery is beautiful. I think no need to enter the house/church  just enjoy the surroundings.
It is a nice short stroll from the parking lot to the church. For Korean drama lovers  I guess. I am not really into it. If you are short for time in Jeju  do give this a miss.

It is quite nice to visit the grounds of this place. Lots of pictures (on cardboards!!) opportunities. But the walk along the trail itself is really quite nice. Great photo view of the sea as the background.

I love the church in the all-in house. it is really beautiful and you would be able to have nice pic taking over there especially if you are a couple .This place is a MUSt if you are a huge korean fan. If you are not  skip this place

Being Australian  we had never heard of All In but were taken here on our tour. We didn't go into the museum but did walk by it along the coast track to the lighthouse. Scenery was very nice. This area is called Seopjikoji on the Jeju maps.
I think we were the only ones there. All explanations in koreAn. Staff are so bored. Could have been made into an interesting experience for children. My son was bored.

It's fun about this place. Entrance fees 12 000 won per person. There's is a show every hour about 15mins each show. But one thing need to highlight is  the explanation are all in Korean words. So for foreigner like us may have difficulties on understand the instructions on the activities. But so far I very enjoy. Is good for indoor visit especially during raining day.

We went as a couple  not expecting much  but this place was really fun! Lots of little experiments to do with electricity  plasma  light. The "tesla coil music orchestra" was impressive... or did I just got high on the ozone? Even the arcade games upstairs were great.We ended up staying for more than 2 hours and left only because they were closing down.I only wish they put more effort into the English information/displays. There are little English summaries  but the Korean version always looked way more exhaustive.There also an "organic salad bar" and a black pork restaurant at the facility  but we didn't have time to visit.

We stopped by this museum at the end of a long day because my daughter  who loves science  was begging us to go. We were all pleasantly surprised. There were quite a few hands on displays like static balls  using bikes to light up a display  a few trick eye displays  plasma globes  and of course Tesla coils. The staff were incredibly friendly and although they didn't speak much English they went out of their way to show us around. The Tesla coil music show was quite cool - the coils were used to create different pitches and played both classical and modern music. It took about an hour to go through everything and cost ??0000 for 2 adults and 2 kids. My kids loved it! Great hands on science.
Go when it almost closed  but got a good experienced. Its better if use taxi or car because lil bit hard to find. Closed at 6pm  its better if museum provided more english explanation.

I actually really enjoyed this museum although for me I'd like a little more English to read the displays but there were a lot of different activities to do for people to see how stuff really works it was pretty cool!

Not much to see. Definitely not somewhere to learn about different herbs or flowers. Felt like a tacky photo shoot area - could be fun but only worthwhile in the night time for all the lights set up.Overall the price was not worth it for our group (especially in our raining there). The Cafe wasn't open either by 10ish (although sign says open at 8am). Our guide claimed that they had to open later today because the weather is cold and "therefore they need more time to warm up the herbs for tea.." which is absolutely ridiculous.100% skip this place if the weather isn't ideal.

Many diff types of flowers in all colors. It's called Herb Garden  lots of Rosemary bushes  but no fragrance at all  what a shame.But the whole set up is really something that will not bring me back there again!!

Herb hill located a bit far from town and we having bit hard time searching for the right place. If happen to drive there by urself just key in Herb Dongsan navigation will lead the way. The journey from Seogwipo to this place it's approximately 40mins. There's two different entrance fees charges which is day entry or night entry the charges is 3k differences. Day entry - 9am - 530pm (9000won per person) Night entry - 530pm onwards (12000won per person) Before you get into this lovely place  they you hand you a map of this place which stated 15 Mark points. The park is really good for photography  remember to get ur tripod with you if you travel alone or just couple. =) come in at day time go back at night time so you have two different view of pic. We arrive at 3pm but we told the lady that we wish to stay until 8pm. and they need us to paid 12000 per person. But I personally think that you can pay the day entry price and stay till late night becos no one is checking the ticket when going out from the park. (At least no one check mine ticket although I paid 12000  so your own risk ya. Just a small tips)
Way too many rules. Can't take off masks for photos  there are 3 small waterfalls that you have to pay to see. Don't waste your money. See a waterfall somewhere else in Jeju for free.

This place has great views  beautiful falls  and a cool folk tale about the nymphs or fairies that visit the falls. Not a particularly difficult walk  but if you have trouble with stairs  pace yourself. Only gave it 4 of 5  because the biggest and best falls are not always running. Best views require a visit after the rains. Definitely still a must do while in Jeju. Only need about 1-1.5 hours here.

Cheonjeyeon waterfall is located at the southern tip of Jeju island near Seogwipo-do. It is about 1.5 hours bus ride from the airport. It is called the 3-tier waterfall as it falls over 3 cliffs before ultimately ending up in the ocean. The legend has it that there are 7 nymphs who visit at night to bathe in the ponds. You will also find the Seonimgyo Bridge on your walk to the waterfall which is adorned by the 7 nymphs  beautifully done in metal.A definite must-do while visiting Jeju-do.
Cascade of three waterfalls flowing down a wooded canyon near the sea. Large pedestrian bridge over the canyon

When going into the falls we thought it was just to see the one water fall  the trails lead to several spots and additional falls. It was so gorgeous and a beautiful hike. There was a lot of stairs  and I did see some tiny kids really struggling at the last falls area. The even had a warning sign for elderly and children that the climb was difficult. It was not bad for my family and children but I could see how others may struggle.

Nice place for a short stroll from the pier to the bridge and over to Saeseom Island. We took quite a number of photos of the sea  bridge  and looking inland to Seogwipo Port. We enjoyed the sea breeze  the view of the clear waters and the displays of acrobatic jumping fish in the port. Locals stroll the area and it is a picturesque place to relax for a while. If you're into nature walks you can follow the trail around the island  which is probably small enough for you to complete in an hour or so.You can also take the submarine tour nearby at Seogwipo Port - but do check the weather conditions  our guide told us that the currents and weather play a big part in whether you'll be able to see lots of marine life during your dive.

Try to walk on the bridge and look back at the town  a great view with strong wind during our visit  we also saw some local people came for fishing in the island itself. Nearby area  there is a submarine tour which cost you around KRW100k ....worth a try.

Nice path all with light for evening walk all around the small island with places to sit here and there. An expensive suspended bridge with wood floor goes across  may be a lot for a 30 minutes walk.There is no fee to cross but next to the entry you can buy a trip in submarine. Well! Just nice walk when you stay close by.

It is just before the Jeongban waterfall.Adult  500 won. So why not... It doesn't have many things but OK. I think this museum made for chinese tourists. It's about cooperation between China and Korea. And also includes the history of the two countries.

this park is right next to Jeongbang Waterfalls  and only costs 500 SKW. We spent an hour there reading up the interesting story of how Xu Fu  the elixir who was said to have stopped here while his envoy with 500 (3000) boys and girls set sail in search for immortal medicine for the Qin Emperor in 219BC. He was said to have left inscriptions on the cliff next to the waterfall marking his presence there.

Seobok was born in 255 B.C. In what is now present day Yongkou city of Shandong province China. That is why there is Taesan square stone donated by people's government of Shandong Province  China. There is also a Seobok monument memorial.The story of his journey to the Far East as commanded by Emperor Qinshihuang can be seen from the stone frescos. You can also get more information from the Seobok Exhibition hall. After this  you can proceed to China Park  nice garden
A trickle off a cliff. Don't bother going unless it's in the middle of a torrent; in which case you wouldn't want to be walking.
It was a lucky day cause I could see the fall! A big one right after the rain. Normally there are no water falls but after heavy rain you can see this scenery!

Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.It was really nice  I recommend it.It's not a waterfall all year around  some people say they didn't find a waterfall  I did though.Visited in Summer of 2015

A lovely puppy greets you at the start of the walk! You walk past a lovely stone house on the left and the dry riverbed on the right. They have well built stairs to the falls. At this time of year there are no falls - due to lack of rain  however there is a lovely pond at the bottom and the ability to climb down the rock's and close to the water. A lovely place to sit and contemplate! Don't recommend kissing the kissing cave...a blarney stone it's not haha!

The answer is of course when there is no water. Even though it was raining  it wasn't raining enough to produce a waterfall. Still a pretty spot with a pleasant walk past orange blossom scented orchards.
You should have a look at this place  look good as your background photo  it is pretty loud when it works.
Nice place to walk and eat  nearby Gimnyeong beach  few restaurant beside this .  we settle our meal at Jenchimang Restaurant
With 20-30 Wind Power Plants on both sides of the road. It is supposed to be an enclosed private areas  but it is not fenced. Can only go with a car or rented cab.

The only one of dolphin experiential theme park in Korea.Enjoy the nature's present at Marine Park. We are trying for people to feel what is the nature's present through communion with dolphins. We hope you to experience our programs beyond your imagination. -Programs1.Dolphin Training Experience 2.Dolphin swimming & Snorkeling3.Dolphin Diving4.Dolphin Prenatal Training Project

I visited the African Museum in Jeju Island.First  we could see the performances of people from Ghana.Traditional singing  dancing  and playing musical instruments created an exciting atmosphere.I could learn a little bit about their culture and tradition by listening to the explanation.In the African Museum  you can see sculptures and dolls of various animals living there.It was very fantnstic.It was also fun to take pictures together.If I visit Jeju Island again someday  I want to visit this place again.

Friend and I visited this museum on our first trip to Korea (while on the island of Jeju) and was pleasantly surprised by a great live performance of traditional African dances and drum beats/riddim. The artifacts are also very interesting and place was so big (3 floors) that we didn't have time to view everything.

We took our 27 month old daughter here mostly because she was about to fall asleep on our bike ride and we didn't want to mess up her nap schedule. When you first walk in  they have a walk through of the animals of Africa. Our daughter had a ball naming the animals and learning new ones. We loved the learning experience she got while she stared bright eyed at all the big (and small) animals. She even loved the art and seeing all the different designs (although we admittedly had to go a bit faster than normal through the rest of the museum). For this being an unplanned stop  we were thrilled we did. What a nice addition to our vacation.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) I visited there for watching about Africa's culture  but the contents was not sufficient to me. The animal was made by doll  and the exhibits was just displayed without subject  I think. But the performance by Senegal's band was excellent. The music was very excited. If there was no performance  I could not award high marks.

Exotic Jeju Island is known for many things: the majestic Hallasan--the massive shield volcano that formed the island and the highest point in South Korea; its mandarin groves; persimmon-dyed galot fashions; the sturdy Jeju ma horses  descended from the ponies of Mongol invaders; tasty black pork; and the iconic haenyeo women divers. But most visitors would not expect to find a Museum of African Art there. And  it's pretty darn good! Located in a massive structure modeled after the mud-brick Great Mosque of Djenne  the museum offers photo-ops galore in its Safari section  although the animals are of the stuffed variety. Very popular with children and couples. The upper floors house a respectable collection of African artifacts and photographs by Kim Jung Man. There is also a great gift shop. But  I have saved the best for last...the live performance of African folk music and dance. The group  Zalia from Senegal  featured lots of drumming  and audience members also got a drumming lesson and a chance to play along on one song. All in all  a quality experience...and a surprising one.

The performance itself is worth the price of admission. Make sure you arrive before one of the three showtimes during the day. They provide drums and you can jam along with the performers. I find this satisfying when you have so many museums in area feigning novelty. So again  If you can get your toddlers away from the stuffed animals  then there is a rewarding human element waiting on the bottom floor.
Visited during a weekend and it is full of life. A lively market that sells local produce with a handful of restaurants within the market. Worth a short visit if you are around the area.

This market is small compared to many others in bigger Korean cities.Anyway  Seogwipo is just a small part of Jeju Island. Can't expect too much.However  the markets in Korea are all too familiar & very similar. In every city  you will never fail to find such markets - supposed it's a culture thing.

Not that easy to find foods for muslim  but if you are not strict the muslim-friendly will do for you if you ask around what theyre put inside.. i looked around the musling speaking person to guide me on this. This one kind Korean salesgirl helped me on this. ^^ so please dont be shy to ask around yaa..^^

The market gets busy after lunch and into the night around 9pm. You can find all sorts of food options and souvenirs in this market...from street foods  to hand-made mochi  to yummy waffles  to restaurant food... There are many cosmetic stores around the market  where you can get cheap facial masks and reasonably priced "volcanic clay mask" jars - a must-purchase in Jeju!

There is a lot of food at this market. From snacks to proper meal. You can buy fresh fruits and souvenirs at this market too. The market is 5 mins walking distance from Artstay hotel. Sashimi is also available at this market.

I went to Jeju after spending 6 days in Seoul. After Namdaemun  Myeondong  Hongdae and many undergeound shopping malls naturally Maeil Oleh Oleh did not excite me. Mainly targeting tourist business and restaurants amd stuff is not cheap there.

This place is considered clean for a local market. Mixture of raw fresh food and cooked food stores. We came here at around 10am and a number of cooked food stores are already open. Nice experience walking around and eating street food along the way. There are benches around for you to sit and have your food. Market closes at 8.30pm.

The street food stalls at night were awesome in the market. However all the good one has long lines and slow moving as most of them are cooking in front of you. Not knowing which one is the best  we choose to join the crowd and stand in line with others and skipped the other with short lines. Parking is terrible even Google Maps shows many nearby parking lots. We tried two separate lots and both were full. Instead of waiting someone to pull out  I ended up parking on the side of nearby street and walked to the market.
Market sell many jeju souvenir   fresh fruit from jeju special orange fruit a live seafoodMust try some local street food

There are a lot of food choices in the market  especially a lot of shops selling the Jeju oranges and Jeju orange juice. You can easily get souvenirs from the market. Most of the shop keepers can speak English/Mandarin. There is a free car park just 1 min on foot from the market  another one with charge right inside the market.

This place offers specialty items/ food of jeju. Vendors are cash only and they offer samples. There are snack stalls and a couple of restaurants inside. One restaurant even have an English translation on it.

This market sell all sort of things from fresh seafood to chocolate. We bought those chocolate souvenier from here. There are many shops selling similar item.One can also buy various ready to eat food (street food kind) and there are restaurants too. One thing to take note is that dustbin is rare  so you may want to bring a plastic bag to throw your litter.

Just visited the market at 12 in the afternoon and felt quite underwhelmed. The market was quiet. There were stalls selling seafood  vegetables and fruits. The food alley wasn't very happening. Tracked down the ahjuma that sold hallabong pancakes  after biting into it  it tasted so so. After hunting for lunch we walked past the market again and noticed more people. Perhaps we visited at the wrong time.

They sell everything here from cooked food  raw food  pots and pans  clothes etc.The food like fried chicken and ttokpokki are a little bit on the expensive side compared to Seoul. Public buses are abundant so you don't have to take taxi all the time.

I have seen many Korean Markets in the course of my 18 days in korea. To be honest  no market have truly captured my attention. You can go to any traditional market in any state of S.K and you wouldn't be missing out. My advice for any Korean Traditional Market in general:- Go to any market that is decently sized that is convenient to travel to from your accomodation. - Take note that they do not have rubbish bins there most of the time and you'd have to return your trash to the store which you have bought the food from. - Be very clear in the number of portions you order as I had a rather awful experience ordering one portion and receiving three person quantity since I had three people.- Go in the morning/day time since most markets will be closing shop by 6pm- The fishcake skewers and the broth are great to enjoy on a cold day. You grab a cup from the stall to get the broth and start eating the oden. Payment will come after you return the sticks to the owner.Lastly  enjoy yourselves in Korea. Learn some basic Korean before you come as you will definitely elevate your experience in Korea. Koreans will always treat you better if they see you making an effort to speak some Korean as all other countries.

This large market is located on the East side of the island. You'll find a variety of places to eats  souvenirs  fresh produces  meats  seafood and variety of other things. It's where the locals to their shopping  as the super markets are small  so it's one stop shopping. After taking a tour on that side of the island  its worth a visit to grab some fresh items if you're tired of eating out all the times  just make sure to bargain with the stall vendors.

It's very much a market for locals but interesting to walk around. There are lots of colourful displays of fruit and vegetables. Dried fish stalls are also common  as are live shellfish and fish tanks where you can choose your purchase. It's a bit smelly in parts  particularly around the meat stalls.
we had so much fun in the market. "ajumas' were very friendly. we already ate alot in the market without spending lot of money. i really liked having korean rice sake

A lot to see. So many kinds of fishes  live or cooked you name it they have it. Reasonable prices are helping you enjoy shopping more! Try street food too. You?™ll love shopping and eating in there but parking is challenging! Very crowded!
Nothing special on this market.. just normal market where u can go buy fresh food and fresh meat.. nothing much here..also things are not cheaper compared to other market.

Not a bad experience. But they typically sell repetition food from one end to the other. The place is clean too. Had a dinner in one of the fish sashimi restaurant  enjoyed very fresh fish sashimi at a reasonable price.

Take this opportunity to eat ?œnon-restaurant??food. Sample things like flambÃ©d cream seafood (in crab shell)  pork trotters  gimbap (Korean rice roll in seaweed)  etc. For those driving there are a couple of public car parks nearby.
Good place to visit to explore traditional Korean Market. Here you can get wide variety of goodies including souvenirs  food items  even live tunas.

If you are looking for variety of street food for consumption  don't go too early for breakfast. Strangely  I thought markets opens early  especially on weekends but I guess I was wrong. Otherwise  I returned in the evening to try out the street food and check out the varieties of fresh food.

Came here looking for lunch. If u r not a fan of sashimi  stay away then. The market primarily sold fresh seafood for the purpose of making sashimi. Easy walking with lots of vendors selling a variety of food - primarily seafood. There was one stall that sold braised pork trotters and very popular. Do watch out for the myriad of vehicles though. From 1926 to the mid 1930s  the Japanese military built a naval airfield and hangar facility covering about 660 000m2. Songaksan Mountain  Dansan Mountain  Mosulbong Peak (187m)  and Sanbangsan Mountain (395m) are called Alter Airfield.

I have spent years reading about WW2 history so it's a sobering experience to walk the same places as the men and women who fought and died in that conflict. Altteureu Airfield was a WW2 Japanese airbase that sits in a strategic corner of Jeju Island  midway between China and Japan. In the 1930s bombing missions were launched from here to Shanghai  later it was a training base. There are 19 remaining concrete hardened shelters sized for a Zero fighter and Jeju has done a good job with preserving the site (even though most of it is active farmland)  adding a large parking lot and bathroom  and placards to explain the history and locate the structures. It's right on the Olle trail so there are many hikers passing through and it's easy to find from the shore road by car.

I am really suprised this place has only few reviews here  it is one of the best things I got to do in Jeju  if you are afraid it's gonna be boring then let me tell you it's not  it's truely a "healing" experience  you leave phone and gadgets at the enterance and you just follow the guide and get far from everything and allow yourself to just rest  well you have to like nature to enjoy this experience for sure. Our guide was unforgettable.

tried the forest healing program last month during my visit to jeju island. Guided by forest therapist we have completed forest healing trail. I can say it really helps me relax the body by focusing on natural noises flowing water  chirping mountain birds  fresh forest air and those Phytoncide!!! oh it just smells so nice >.< we got to try the foot bath and aromatherapy too. the therapist said they also have body bathing tub and aqua line  but since we dont have many time.. maybe next time. I visited this place during summer. As a fan of Zippo  I was AMAZED how Zippo lighters could transfer into some art. It was not only fun place for me but also a fun place for my kids. The location of the museum is fabulous!! There's a beautiful garden with a beach view right outside of the museum  which was great for my whole family. Highly recommend!

If you`re a Zippo lover  this is a must visit spot. Museum locates in the ground floor of a modern seaside building with breathtaking pacific ocean view. There is 2 exhibition halls  one of those displays many special designed zippos in large size  and the other in fact is a zippo shop  you can see and buy different limited edition zippo there and many are designed by local designer.

This is a facility that houses multiple attractions  and they are all basically geared toward separating the tourist from his or her money. Notwithstanding this  our family had a great time spending a couple of hours here. The main attraction appears to be the indoor cart racing track. It's not cheap  around KRW 40 000 for a package that includes 10 minutes on the track and a ticket to the "unique objects" museum. We actually found the items in the museum quite entertaining - objects that trick your eye  weird inventions. The go cart driving was a bit disconcerting (no helmets  no apparent real concern for safety) but in the end it was fun. I was glad I was on the track with just another father-son pair. On the way out  my kid bought carrots for horses that were in a corral  and the guy there was nice enough to take my kid around a lap on the horse (again  no safety gear). My kid was fine but I was glad when both the go cart ride and the horseride finished without any problems.If you are desperate to kill a couple of ours and the weather is bad  this may be a good place to go with tweens or teens. They also offered a "Survival Game" attraction which looked like it was done with laser-tag type guns (not paintball).
